subject: possible brms problem in measurement error (on independent variable)

messages.author: b6fd2925353976cd
messages.subject: possible brms problem in measurement error (on independent variable)
parts:
Hi Paul,

I am trying to fit this model below:

m2Mbrm <- brm(formula = msVOT  ~ 1 + me(cmeanvdur,sestd) + (1 | subject)+(1 | item),
            data = Mdatmerged, 
            family = gaussian(),
            prior = priors,
            warmup = 1000, iter = 2000, 
            chains = 4,
            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95))


The data frame has a single centered mean vowel duration value (cmeanvdur) for each subject, but I have it on authority from a local brms/Stan expert (I leave it as an exercise to guess who that might be) that brms thinks that this predictor was measured for *each* observation, which is obviously false because I have repeated measures from each subject for the dependent variable. So, brms tries to estimate the true vowel duration for each observation, not each subject. In pure Stan I can of course deal with this easily by writing a separate for loop that loops over the subject variable, and I can explicitly specify that each *subject* has a true underlying vowel duration. Does brms have a mechanism for constraining the estimation in this way? My for loop for the Stan model looks like this. I don't write a for-loop but rather specify the true_mvdur indexing by subj id:

Code in pure Stan inside model block:

true_mvdur ~ normal(0, 200);         
  meanvdur ~ normal(true_mvdur, se); // measurement model
  
mu = beta[1] + u[subj] + w[item] + beta[2] * true_mvdur[subj];

How do I achieve this in brms?

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] possible brms problem in measurement error (on independent variable)
parts:
The solution I proposed earlier today doesn't make sense in your case. brms is not yet able to express a variable with measurement error when multiple rows in the data belong to the same true score.

I should have read your model more carefully in the first place...

If you like, please feel free to open an issue on github (https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues) so that I don't forget about making this possible at some point.
